Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Dan Choudhry, DOB: Not recorded, Gender: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded, Address: Not recorded
- Referring GP: Not recorded, Practice: Not recorded, Practice Address: Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Acute gastroenteritis — provisional diagnosis (acute viral gastroenteritis most likely per DDx)
- Secondary: Anxiety / worry about work attendance and reluctance to take time off (patient reported disliking taking time off work and trying to attend despite illness)
- Tertiary: Risk of dehydration due to profuse watery diarrhoea and reduced urine frequency

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Paracetamol PRN (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Allergies/ADRs: No known drug allergies (patient reports none)
- Past Medical History: Reported otherwise fit and well; no chronic conditions recalled

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: Not recorded
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalisations): Not recorded
- Family History: Father with stage 3 colon cancer

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives with mother and sister; brother does not live with him
- Social Support: Lives with family but reports not discussing symptoms in detail with mother/sister; prefers to "deal with these things"
- Occupation/Education: Employed in an office role in Central London (works in government)
- Alcohol Use: Occasional alcohol; heavier episodic drinking once or twice per month with friends
- Smoking/Substance Use: Social smoker (occasional)
- Key Stressors: Concern about missing work / reluctance to take time off; family history of serious illness (father with colon cancer); concurrent illness in brother

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Coherent, conversational, engaged on telehealth call; cooperative (no abnormal behaviour documented)
- Mood & Affect: Reports "feeling not so great" (low mood/distress related to current physical illness). Affect appropriate to content
- Speech & Thought: Speech coherent, goal-directed; no formal thought disorder documented
- Perception: No hallucinations or perceptual disturbance reported

Cognition:
- Orientation: Oriented to name and age (provided correctly)
- Attention/Concentration: Able to follow questions and provide relevant information during call
- Memory: Short-term/long-term memory not formally assessed; no objective memory deficits documented
- Insight & Judgement: Demonstrates insight into symptoms and their possible cause; expresses desire to continue working despite illness (judgement intact but may increase risk of worsening dehydration)

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Not recorded
- Appetite: Had lunch today but stool remained loose; appetite otherwise not documented
- Motivation/Energy: Not recorded
- Anxiety Symptoms: Worry about taking time off work; prefers to cope alone and not discuss with family

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: No suicidal ideation, self-harm or risk to others reported (Not recorded for active ideation)
- Protective Factors: Lives with family, employed, able to access pharmacy/over-the-counter ORS (Dioralyte), able to purchase paracetamol
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low (based on no reported self-harm/suicidal ideation; physical risk from dehydration noted)
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: No chronic medical or psychiatric history recorded; family stressor (father with advanced colon cancer).
- Precipitating factors: Likely infectious exposure (brother with similar diarrhoeal illness); onset ~3 days ago with profuse watery diarrhoea, crampy central/lower abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting after milk.
- Perpetuating factors: Continued attendance at work despite symptoms; not hydrating adequately (reports fluids passing straight through, decreased urine frequency); reluctance to disclose symptoms to family limiting immediate support.
- Protective factors: Co-habitation with family, ability to obtain ORS and paracetamol, likely self-limited course per clinician and DDx.
- Integrated formulation: A probable acute viral gastroenteritis episode is causing physical symptoms and transient distress/anxiety about work attendance. Physical illness with high stool output places the patient at risk for dehydration; psychosocial factors (work reluctance, limited sharing with family) may impede rest and adequate fluid replacement. Management focuses on rehydration, symptomatic relief, safety-netting, and brief psychoeducation regarding work absence and monitoring for deterioration.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Acute gastroenteritis (provisional — likely viral)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Resolution or marked improvement of diarrhoea, nausea and abdominal pain within days
  - Maintain hydration and avoid hospital presentation
  - Return to work when clinically appropriate
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Prevent or treat dehydration
  - Provide symptomatic relief and clear safety-netting for escalation
  - Monitor for red flags requiring investigation or admission
- Actions (Patient):
  - Increase oral fluids; obtain and use Oral Rehydration Solution (Dioralyte) as advised
  - Follow clear fluids and soft diet (soup, mash) initially, advance as tolerated
  - Take paracetamol for fever/pain as needed (dose/route/frequency per packaging / clinician advice)
  - Avoid alcohol until recovery
  - Monitor urine output, dizziness, worsening abdominal pain, bloody stools, persistent high fever or inability to tolerate fluids
  - Contact GP/clinic if no improvement within 48 hours or sooner for red flags
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide advice on ORS, hydration and symptomatic management (paracetamol acceptable)
  - Safety-net: patient instructed to recontact if symptoms persist >48 hours or if signs of dehydration or systemic illness occur
  - Arrange urgent assessment/face-to-face review and vital signs if dehydration suspected (reduced urine, hypotension, altered consciousness) or if red flags present
  - Consider prescription or further investigations only if clinical deterioration or features suggest bacterial/invasive infection (blood in stool, high fever)

Secondary Problem: Anxiety / worry about work attendance
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce worry about taking time off and feel supported to rest while unwell
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Provide reassurance and practical advice about work absence and recovery timeframe
  - Support reasonable decisions regarding sick leave if patient unfit for work
- Actions (Patient):
  - Consider informing employer if unwell and unable to work; prioritise rest and rehydration
  - Use basic self-care and ask for family support as needed
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide reassurance that acute gastroenteritis is usually self-limited; advise avoiding work while symptomatic and infectious
  - Offer fit note / sick certification if patient is unfit to work (if requested and clinically indicated)
  - If anxiety about work persists or functional impairment continues after physical recovery, consider brief referral to counseling or primary care mental health services (Not recorded whether requested)

Tertiary Problem: Risk of dehydration
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Maintain adequate hydration and prevent complications
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Early recognition and treatment of dehydration; arrange escalation if needed
- Actions (Patient):
  - Monitor urine output and symptoms (dizziness, dry mouth, reduced urine)
  - Use ORS as recommended; seek urgent care for lightheadedness, fainting, minimal or no urine, persistent vomiting
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Reassess within 48 hours or sooner if deterioration; measure vitals and consider blood tests/IV fluids if moderate-severe dehydration suspected
  - Provide clear instructions on when to attend emergency services

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Likely diagnosis (gastroenteritis), expected course, hydration (use of Dioralyte/ORS), diet recommendations (clear fluids, soft diet), paracetamol for fever/pain, avoidance of alcohol, safety-netting and when to seek urgent care
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Signs of moderate-severe dehydration (markedly reduced urine output, dizziness, lightheadedness, fainting)
  - High or persistent fever
  - Severe or increasing abdominal pain
  - Bloody stools or persistent vomiting preventing fluid intake
  - No improvement after 48 hours
- Coping Strategies:
  - Rest and gradual return to activity as tolerated
  - Prioritise hydration and simple nourishing foods (soup, mash)
  - Request workplace support / short-term absence to recover
  - Ask for help from family members for groceries/medication if needed

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not recorded
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded
- Review Date: Safety-net review within 48 hours (patient instructed to call earlier if red flags)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Acute viral gastroenteritis (e.g., norovirus) — Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Acute 3-day history of frequent watery diarrhoea, crampy abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting and household contact (brother) with similar self-limited illness.
- Bacterial foodborne gastroenteritis (e.g., enterotoxigenic E. coli, Salmonella, Campylobacter) — Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Can present with profuse watery diarrhoea, cramping and subjective fever; possible shared exposure with brother could support this.
- Secondary lactose intolerance (post-infectious lactase deficiency) — Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Vomiting/greater symptoms after milk and recent enteric illness can cause transient lactase deficiency worsening dairy-associated symptoms.

Quality checks
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Objective vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate) — Not recorded
  - Weight / baseline measures — Not recorded
  - Formal mental health history (previous diagnoses, previous treatments) — Not recorded
  - Explicit patient consent for this documented plan — Not recorded
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None significant. DDx emphasizes likely viral gastroenteritis which aligns with clinician's recorded assessment.
- Transcript quality notes:
  - Telehealth audio-only encounter; patient could hear clinician but could not see clinician. No physical examination or vital signs were documented due to remote consultation. Dialogue complete though occasional short pauses; some minor conversational disfluency.
